chat.help.title: Chat help
chat.help.askDesc: The standard mode. Claude asks permission before EVERY action that touches your system (editing files, running commands): a card appears and you approve or deny each one.
chat.help.editsDesc: Claude can edit and create files without asking; everything else (terminal commands, network, etc.) still asks for permission. Handy once you trust the direction of the work.
chat.help.allDesc: Advanced acceptance: Claude runs ABSOLUTELY everything without asking — commands, edits, network. It's the riskiest mode (that's why it confirms when you turn it on); use it only when you fully trust the task and want zero friction.
chat.help.planDesc: Claude touches nothing: it just reads the project and drafts a work plan. Ideal to explore an idea or see what it would do before letting it loose.
chat.help.modesFoot: You can change mode at any time; it applies from the next action. The selector color marks the risk: green = controlled · amber = medium · red = accepts everything.
chat.help.iconsIntro: Tools no longer take over the thread: each work block is summarized by a Pac-Man and its tool count. Tap it to open the full command, changes, and result in the right panel. Pac-Man moves while the block is active, stops when it finishes, and turns red if anything fails.
chat.help.pacIntro: The header Pac-Man shows the turn state; each block's Pac-Man summarizes its tools. Color and movement show what is happening.
chat.help.pacWorkingDesc: gold, fast chomp: a turn running now
chat.help.pacDelegatingDesc: purple with the intercom icon: waiting for a subagent (Task) or another process to return
chat.help.pacWaitingDesc: green, slow blink: waiting for your message or your decision
chat.help.pacErrorDesc: red and still: at least one tool in the block failed
chat.help.pacDormantDesc: gray and still: every tool in the block finished successfully
chat.redo.text: 🤔 I think a stronger model would do this better.
chat.help.intro: Chat is where you talk with the assistant and see every action it takes on your project. You can choose how much permission to grant, attach context, and follow the work as it happens.
chat.help.first.title: Getting started
chat.help.first.step1: Choose the permission mode from the header selector.
chat.help.first.step2: Type or dictate your request; if needed, tap Attach or Reference package to add context.
chat.help.first.step3: Tap Send or press Enter. Use Shift+Enter to add a line without sending.
chat.help.first.step4: Answer any questions and permission requests; tap each block's Pac-Man to open its tool details in the side panel.
chat.help.first.step5: To cut off a response in progress, tap Stop and confirm.
chat.help.controlsLegend.title: Legend · controls
chat.help.controlsLegend.menu.name: Menu
chat.help.controlsLegend.menu.desc: opens the side panel on small screens
chat.help.controlsLegend.attach.name: Attach
chat.help.controlsLegend.attach.desc: adds files to the next message
chat.help.controlsLegend.package.name: Package
chat.help.controlsLegend.package.desc: brings in a reference from another session
chat.help.controlsLegend.send.name: Send
chat.help.controlsLegend.send.desc: sends the message or starts an action
chat.help.controlsLegend.stop.name: Stop
chat.help.controlsLegend.help.name: Help
chat.help.legQuestionDesc: asks you to choose or write an answer
chat.help.viz.title: Charts and diagrams
chat.help.viz.charts: When the AI presents quantitative data, charts may be drawn directly inside the message.
chat.help.viz.mermaid: Mermaid diagrams use the full width; the “Expand” button opens them in a larger view for exploring complex structures and flows.
chat.help.viz.source: Below each visualization, “View chart data” or “View Mermaid code” expands the exact source so you can copy it.
chat.help.viz.tokens: Charts are drawn in your browser and use NO tokens.
chat.help.tandem.title: Tandem mode
chat.help.tandem.what.v: Claude (Opus with high effort) reasons, plans, and verifies; Codex GPT-5.6 Sol with high effort implements code changes.
chat.help.tandem.badge.v: The header shows “Tandem” when active. Change the model from the conversation menu in Sessions, not from this badge.
chat.help.tandem.inactive.v: The choice changed, but the current engine started earlier. Use “Reopen for changes” from the Sessions menu.
chat.help.tandem.parallel.v: Claude can launch several Codex delegations at once when they touch separate files. Never run two delegations against the same file in parallel: they may overwrite each other.
chat.help.tandem.restart.v: Each delegation runs in its own process and persists to disk. It keeps running if the web interface restarts, and Claude can recover its status and result afterward.
chat.help.continuity.title: Continuity and autonomy
chat.help.continuity.runner.k: New code and a live runner
chat.help.continuity.runner.v: A live runner keeps the code it loaded at startup. To pick up new changes, use “Reopen for changes” from the Sessions menu; context is preserved.
chat.help.continuity.ball.v: The final line is a contract, not decoration: when the assistant ends with “🎾 Pelota: MÍA”, the system hands control back to it and the chat continues on its own without waiting for another message from you.
chat.help.buttons.title: Buttons and actions
chat.help.buttons.popout.name: Pop out
chat.help.buttons.popout.desc: Opens this conversation in its own window without panels, which is useful for split screen. It is the same conversation: it also stays open here, and anything you type in either window goes to the same turn.
chat.help.buttons.menu.v: On mobile, opens navigation for sessions and tools.
chat.help.buttons.world.v: Shows which project and accounts this conversation uses; informational only.
chat.help.buttons.flow.v: Shows approximate Claude and Codex activity and tokens; informational and only shown when applicable.
chat.help.buttons.pacman.v: Summarizes whether the chat is working, delegating, or waiting for your message.
chat.help.buttons.model.v: Shows AutoTux, Tandem, or the forced model and effort. It is not a selector: change it from Sessions.
chat.help.buttons.mode.v: Changes how much autonomy the assistant has starting with the next action.
chat.help.buttons.attach.v: Uploads up to 8 images, PDFs, text files, or other files; you can also paste or drag them in. Attaching, removing, or previewing files uses no tokens; usage starts when you send the message containing them.
chat.help.buttons.package.v: Opens a session search and inserts the selected reference into your message. Shortcut: F5. Searching or inserting uses 0 tokens; sending the message does use tokens.
chat.help.buttons.input.v: Type or dictate. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. “/” opens command completion: use the arrow keys, Tab or Enter to select, and Esc to close.
chat.help.buttons.send.v: Sends the message and puts the assistant to work; that work consumes tokens.
chat.help.buttons.stop.v: Interrupts the response in progress after confirmation. It does not start another turn or undo completed actions.
chat.help.buttons.permission.v: Tap the chip to expand the exact tool, command, or diff, then approve or reject that action. Dangerous commands start expanded.
chat.help.buttons.tool.v: Opens the side panel with each tool's command, file, result, or error. Tap it again—or use ✕ / Esc—to close it.
chat.help.buttons.rawpanel.v: Takes up the right third of the chat; on phones it opens nearly full-screen. It only shows tools from the block you selected.
chat.help.buttons.answer.v: Choose an option or type another answer; Send is enabled once all are complete. Cancel rejects the question. Sending lets the turn continue, and that continuation uses tokens.
chat.help.buttons.pending.v: An instruction created from Aduana remains editable in the composer and does not run by itself. Send starts a token-using turn; Discard removes it without using tokens.
chat.help.buttons.retry.v: If a stronger-model suggestion appears, you decide whether to redo the last turn; it never switches on its own. Retry consumes tokens.
chat.help.warning.title: Watch out
chat.help.warning.text: “All” can run commands, edit files, and use the network without asking again. Stop prevents further work but does not undo completed actions; review the side-panel details before approving anything sensitive.

chat.help.sala.title: Aduana room
chat.help.sala.intro: A shared conversation where people coordinate and call the AI only when the group decides.
chat.help.sala.people.cucho: The room’s AI is called Cucho. Writing @cucho marks that message as a question for Cucho, but that alone does not wake Cucho up: you still need to tap the button. When there are marked questions, the button sends only those and the rest of the conversation waits for the next cut.
chat.help.sala.indexBlurb: Shared conversation, cuts, participants, and token usage.
chat.help.sala.what.title: What is a room?
chat.help.sala.what.text: Aduana is a collaborative room where several people share one thread and talk among themselves. The AI starts silent: human messages do not call it, and it only speaks after someone taps the cut button.
chat.help.sala.first.title: Getting started in the room
chat.help.sala.first.step1: Write a message and tap Send: it travels through the say channel, appears in the shared thread, and costs 0 tokens; it does not call the AI.
chat.help.sala.first.step2: Wait or keep talking until you have the context you need. The counter shows how many messages were posted since the last cut.
chat.help.sala.first.step3: Tap ✦ Send to AI when you want to start a turn. If it is busy, the cut remains queued.
chat.help.sala.first.step4: Follow the answer in the same thread; every participant can see the full conversation.
chat.help.sala.controls.title: Room controls
chat.help.sala.controls.compose.v: Add files or a reference to another session, then post the say. Preparing that content costs 0 tokens; it waits for the next cut.
chat.help.sala.controls.stop.v: During an AI turn, asks for confirmation and stops further work without undoing completed actions. Only the person who made the cut—or the owner as backup—can decide.
chat.help.sala.controls.acta.v: Tap the heading to expand or collapse it; the warning tells you when it may be out of date.
chat.help.sala.legend.title: Room legend
chat.help.sala.legend.ai.name: Send to AI
chat.help.sala.legend.ai.desc: sends the accumulated conversation; if there are @cucho questions, it sends only those and leaves the rest waiting
chat.help.sala.legend.cut.name: Cut
chat.help.sala.legend.cut.desc: marks exactly which part of the conversation the AI received
chat.help.sala.legend.origin.name: Room entry
chat.help.sala.legend.origin.desc: the thread marker shows which world the conversation came from and who brought it
chat.help.sala.legend.subsala.name: Sub-room
chat.help.sala.legend.subsala.desc: Cucho opened a child room; tap the line to open or focus it
chat.help.sala.legend.eco.name: Room-to-room notice
chat.help.sala.legend.eco.desc: a message exchanged by a child room and its parent; tap the heading to open the other room
chat.help.sala.legend.colors.name: Colors
chat.help.sala.people.title: People, mentions, and reading
chat.help.sala.people.identity: Each participant has their own avatar and color. That color repeats in their name, messages, and mentions; consecutive messages from the same author are grouped into one block.
chat.help.sala.people.reply: The AI response shows who it is addressing. If it replies to several people, you will see all of their colors.
chat.help.sala.people.mentions: Type @ to open the participant list and mention someone. The person you mention gets a stronger alert than the regular “new messages” notice.
chat.help.sala.people.unread: The “new messages” divider marks where you started reading this time. It remains in the thread even after the unread counter is cleared.
chat.help.sala.people.reactions: React with 👍, ❓, or 🔴 to align without writing. Reactions use no tokens and never enter the AI context; a written message waits for the next cut.
chat.help.sala.people.quoteReply: The fourth button in that row replies with a quote. Tap the visible quote to jump to the original. Posting the reply costs 0 tokens like any say; it waits and only becomes paid context when someone makes the next cut.
chat.help.sala.minutes.title: Room minutes
chat.help.sala.minutes.text: The minutes above the thread track agreements, pending items, and open questions. The AI updates them at each cut when there is something new to record; the room warns you if they have gone too long without an update.
chat.help.sala.permissions.title: Permissions and ownership
chat.help.sala.permissions.owner.v: Only the room owner sets the permission mode. A guest can never change it, even if they can see the selector.
chat.help.sala.permissions.all.v: A room can run in All (bypassPermissions), but only by the owner's explicit choice. It accepts commands, edits, and network access without asking and carries the same high risk as a regular chat.
chat.help.sala.orchestrate.title: Orchestrate a response
chat.help.sala.orchestrate.text: Orchestrate creates a new conversation in the world you choose and leaves the text waiting in its composer for review or editing. Nothing runs until you open that conversation and send the message.
chat.help.sala.tokens.title: What uses tokens
chat.help.sala.tokens.people.v: Costs 0 tokens: it is broadcast and saved as internal conversation. It only becomes paid context if someone later makes a cut.
chat.help.sala.tokens.reactions.v: Uses no tokens: reactions never enter the next cut or travel to the AI as context.
chat.help.sala.tokens.quoteReply.v: Costs 0 tokens when posted; as a say, it waits for the next cut. The visible quote links to the original message.
chat.help.sala.tokens.ai.v: Uses tokens: it starts a turn with everything accumulated since the last cut.
chat.help.sala.tokens.orchestrate.v: Uses no tokens by itself. Usage begins later only if you send the message from the new conversation.
chat.help.sala.warning.title: Watch out
chat.help.sala.warning.text: AI turns are charged to the room host, no matter who taps the cut button. Guests see the entire shared thread, including earlier messages and AI answers.
